text:
Ravi Menon: Kicking off architecture review Qs for auto-rollback SLO integration. Main things I want to resolve today:
1) Monitor outage / stale data behavior: fail-open vs fail-closed (and whether per-tier).
2) Guardrails to avoid cascading rollbacks (global + per-tenant rate limits).
3) Dependency failure modes (telemetry query latency, label mismatch, partial region outages).

Jordan Lee: +1. The policy engine currently assumes we can always get a verdict (healthy/unhealthy). Need a third state: `unknown` when data is missing/stale.

Ethan Park: On (1) my gut: do NOT rollback on unknown. Rolling back on missing data is how we end up flapping during monitoring incidents.

Sean Gallagher: SRE POV: default should be “no automated rollback unless we’re confident.” If monitor pipeline is broken, rollback could mask the real incident and create churn. So: unknown => hold traffic split steady, page/ticket depending on severity.

Miles Thornton: Agree. But we should talk about “fail-closed” in the sense of “freeze rollout progression” (don’t increase canary %) when unknown. That’s different from rollback.

Allison Grant: +100. We should separate:
- Rollout step controller (can it advance?)
- Rollback executor (should it revert?)
Unknown should block auto-advance; unhealthy should trigger rollback (if guardrails pass).

Benji Okafor: Implementation detail: monitor client will have cached results + staleness TTL. If upstream 5xx or timeout, we’ll serve last known value up to TTL, then mark unknown.

Nadia Rahman: Please make TTL explicit + metric-specific. Latency SLO queries can lag by 1-2m in some regions (ingestion delay). If we set TTL too low we’ll churn into unknown constantly.

Jordan Lee: Proposal:
- `evaluation_window`: e.g. 5m
- `max_signal_delay`: default 3m (configurable)
- `stale_after`: evaluation_window + max_signal_delay
If last datapoint older than `stale_after` => unknown.

Ravi Menon: Cool. For (1) then: do we want any scenario where unknown => rollback? (e.g., “fail-closed” for high-risk customers?)

Sean Gallagher: I’d strongly recommend no. If you want extra safety for Tier-0, use stricter “advance gating” + manual approval. But don’t auto-rollback on missing signal.

Mina Haddad: Routing side concern: if we freeze the traffic split on unknown, do we also stop any scheduled progressive delivery? (We have cron-ish steps)

Ethan Park: Yes. If verdict=unknown, controller should not change split. That includes auto-advance and auto-rollback. It should emit an event + surface in Console.

Allison Grant: We should define alerting: “rollout health unknown due to monitoring outage” should be visible but NOT page the world. Ticket unless it persists.

Miles Thornton: In game day, one scenario is monitor outage. Success criteria: no rollback, but the rollout should pause and oncall should get a clear reason + link.

Jordan Lee: Ok switching to (2) rate limiting global rollbacks. We’ve seen correlated incidents where many routes in a region spike simultaneously. If every tenant rolls back we amplify control-plane writes + routing changes.

Ravi Menon: Exactly. Need a circuit breaker: max rollbacks per time window globally and per-dimension (region/tier).

Benji Okafor: I can add:
- per-tenant cooldown (already planned)
- per-controller-instance token bucket (to limit API writes)
But we also need cross-instance coordination if we run multiple controllers.

Ethan Park: We can centralize via control plane DB row lock / lease. E.g. “rollback budget” table keyed by {region, tier} with counters per 10m window.

Miles Thornton: Be careful: if DB is unhealthy, you don’t want this to block legitimate rollback. But also don’t want runaway.

Sean Gallagher: SRE ask: prefer deterministic + auditable behavior. If budget is exhausted, the event should say “rollback suppressed due to rate limit” and still page/ticket so humans can intervene.

Jordan Lee: Concrete numbers to start?
- Per-tenant: max 1 rollback / 30m (configurable)
- Per region+tier: max 10 rollbacks / 10m (hardcoded default)
- Global: max 50 rollbacks / 10m
We can tune post-launch.

Allison Grant: Also add “must be worse than baseline” guardrail for correlated incidents. If baseline version is also bad (same SLO breach), rollback doesn’t help. That should reduce mass rollbacks.

Nadia Rahman: On that: baseline comparison requires fetching baseline metrics too. That doubles query load. If we do it, cache aggressively and make sure queries are templated/label-normalized.

Benji Okafor: We can structure as:
1) Fetch candidate SLO result (canary version)
2) If unhealthy and min-traffic met, fetch baseline (stable version)
3) Rollback only if candidate is worse by margin (e.g. +X ms p95, or error rate ratio)
So baseline query is only on “pre-rollback” path.

Ravi Menon: (3) dependency failure modes. Let’s enumerate what can go wrong and expected behavior:
- Monitor API timeout
- Monitor returns partial series / NaN
- Label mismatch (route/model/region/tier tags missing)
- Telemetry ingestion delay
- Routing API fails mid-rollback

Jordan Lee: For monitor API timeout: return unknown. Include reason: `monitor_fetch_timeout`.

Allison Grant: For partial series/NaN: treat as unknown unless we have enough points to compute SLO. We should log “insufficient points” with min datapoints requirement.

Nadia Rahman: Label mismatch is the scary one. You might be querying the wrong thing and thinking it’s healthy/unhealthy. Should fail to unknown if required labels are missing.

Benji Okafor: +1. We can validate monitor identity contract on read: required tags present, else unknown + emit metric `slo_monitor_invalid{reason="missing_label"}`.

Marcus Lin: Security/compliance nit: any “unknown due to invalid monitor config” should be in audit trail? Maybe not as an audit event, but at least in event stream accessible in Console (so customers can see why automation didn’t trigger).

Ethan Park: For routing API failure mid-rollback: executor must be idempotent + transactional-ish. E.g. write desired state first, then apply. If apply fails, retry with idempotency key.

Miles Thornton: Also: if rollback partially applies (some shards updated), we need “reconcile loop” to converge. Otherwise you end up with split-brain traffic.

Jordan Lee: Control plane pattern we’ve used: store “rollback intent” record with state machine: PENDING -> APPLYING -> APPLIED/FAILED. Reconciler re-drives APPLYING.

Sean Gallagher: And oncall needs to see that. If it’s stuck in APPLYING, that’s a page (not a ticket).

Ravi Menon: So summarizing proposed decisions:
- Verdict states: healthy / unhealthy / unknown.
- Unknown: freeze rollout (no advance, no rollback). Emit event + surface in Console. Ticket if persists; page only if APPLYING stuck or widespread.
- Rollback guarded by: min traffic, warmup grace, baseline worse-than check, cooldown.
- Rate limits: per-tenant cooldown + global/region+tier budgets. If suppressed, log reason and notify.
- Dependency failures: monitor fetch issues => unknown; invalid monitor identity => unknown; routing failures => executor retries + reconciler.

Allison Grant: Works for me. Please make sure ADR explicitly calls out “freeze vs rollback” so we don’t bikeshed ‘fail-closed’ wording later.

Miles Thornton: + add to game day scenarios: (a) monitor outage => unknown + pause; (b) region incident where baseline also bad => no rollback; (c) routing API failure => stuck APPLYING and reconciler recovers.

Benji Okafor: Action items from me:
- Add `unknown` verdict plumbing + reason codes
- Implement staleness logic (evaluation_window + max_signal_delay)
- Sketch rate limit storage approach (DB budget table + token bucket)

Jordan Lee: I’ll draft the policy semantics section for unknown + suppression reasons. Ravi, I’ll drop it in the ADR doc for review.

Ravi Menon: Great. Please @ me on the ADR draft. I want to make sure we’re crisp on “no rollback on unknown” and on the cross-instance rate limit mechanism.
